_comment: Writes the three timelines of the full product demo (under 5 minutes, no slides), Video.mp4 in Group19.zip: Part A. Generated by demo/make_timeline_demo.py; record with REPLAY_STEP_PACE=0.35.

steps.say: ThreadPilot, the general manager’s co-pilot. She signs in with her name, so saved records show who wrote them.
Before she is at her desk, it emails her unasked, in the daytime only. This is the email, word for word.
When is it due? The system works it out: seven o’clock, three urgent items. We jump to two seconds before.
06:59:58 … 07:00:00: the check fires. One email to the manager, three urgent items, never sent twice. (Offline replay: recorded, not delivered.)
She opens the app. The day is on one screen: red, 8 overdue, assembly below normal for 6 days, 3 decisions.
Each decision has one button. “Review options” runs the queue simulation for ORD-029, which will miss today.
Moving ORD-029 up saves it 5 days but adds 11 to six other orders, so it recommends keeping the current order.
Drafted before she asks: the two stalled orders already have a chase-up, written from the records.
“Review & send” opens the preview: to washing, 9 days idle, 3 days overdue. She reads it and confirms.
Sent and logged. Nothing went out before her click.
